subject: Marketplace procurement: AWS marketplace & PO vs card - next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@lumenai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Marketplace procurement: AWS marketplace & PO vs card - next steps

Hi Alice — thanks again for the call today, really helpful to understand LumenAI's rollout. Quick recap and suggested next steps:

- Summary: LumenAI is evaluating Redwood for inference serving for customer-facing features (chat + embed-based search). Primary procurement drivers: simple procurement path, desire for marketplace (AWS preferred), and flexible billing (PO vs. corporate card).
- Procurement notes you shared: procurement@lumenai.com typically prefers a PO on a 60-day net; legal needs a short SaaS contract (standard SLAs) and security review (SOC 2 + network diagram).

Open questions for us to confirm so we can put together a marketplace-friendly path: 
1) Do you need Redwood to publish on the AWS Marketplace (SaaS Contracts) or would a private contract + invoice/PO be acceptable?
2) If marketplace, do you want the consumption architecture (marketplace metered billing) or a subscription listing?
3) Expected start date and first-year commit (ballpark) so we can prepare a preliminary quote and marketplace listing timeline.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll send a short procurement checklist and an initial quote for both PO (invoice) and AWS Marketplace paths.
- Marissa (cc’d) will share our marketplace listing checklist and sample SaaS contract redlines.
- If procurement would like, we can set a short call with our Partner/Marketplace team to walk the process.

Attaching: redwood-saas-marketplace-qs.pdf (quick checklist for marketplace listings).

Would you be able to introduce me to procurement@lumenai.com directly (if that’s the right inbox) so we can loop them into the checklist?

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.
—
Camila Reyes
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@lumenai.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@lumenai.com
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 10:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace procurement: AWS marketplace & PO vs card - next steps

Hi Camila — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers from my side after chatting with procurement and legal: 

- Marketplace: AWS Marketplace is our preferred path if the listing supports a SaaS Contracts flow (so we can sign via marketplace). That would be ideal from our procurement side.
- Billing: We typically do PO with net-60, but we can use corporate card for an initial POC if needed. For production, PO preferred.
- Contract: Legal will want the standard SaaS contract. We will still run a short review but want to avoid long negotiations.

I’ve looped in procurement (procurement@lumenai.com) — they handle vendor onboarding. Procurement will validate the marketplace process and confirm whether they require a reseller or prefer direct marketplace purchase.

Proposed: procurement, can you confirm whether LumenAI requires a private listing or if a public SaaS listing on AWS Marketplace is ok? Also confirm the central billing entity (LumenAI, Inc.) and any required PO fields.

Thanks,
Alice
Product Ops | LumenAI
alice.chen@lumenai.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@lumenai.com
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.chen@lumenai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace procurement: AWS marketplace & PO vs card - next steps

Hi procurement team — nice to meet you by email. Per Alice’s note, I’m sharing two paths we commonly support:

1) AWS Marketplace (preferred):
   - Redwood lists a SaaS subscription on the AWS Marketplace with SaaS Contracts support.
   - Benefits for you: streamlined purchase/signing via AWS, consolidated billing under the AWS invoice, and standard marketplace terms.
   - Typical timeline: 2–4 weeks for listing + legal review (quicker if you accept standard SaaS contract).

2) Direct PO / Invoice (non-marketplace):
   - Redwood executes a short SaaS purchase agreement; we invoice LumenAI and accept PO with net-60 payment terms.
   - Timeline: can be TBD depending on legal redlines; procurement paperwork often adds 1–3 weeks.

Questions for procurement to confirm so we can prepare the right artifacts:
- If marketplace, do you need meter-based consumption pricing or an annual subscription SKU? (We can provide both.)
- Is there a preferred master purchase order template / required PO fields?
- Any internal vendor registration links we should fill out?

Attaching a draft quote (redwood-catalog-quote-20260221.xlsx) and a short sample SaaS contract + marketplace checklist. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute call with our Marketplace team next week to walk the onboarding steps and timeline.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: procurement@lumenai.com
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Alice Chen <alice.chen@lumenai.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace procurement: AWS marketplace & PO vs card - next steps

Hi Camila/Alice — procurement here. Confirming: LumenAI prefers the AWS Marketplace SaaS Contracts flow (public listing is fine) and will issue a PO for production purchases on net-60 terms. For the POC, we can pay via corporate card to expedite.

Requested next steps from our side:
- Please provide a formal quote for an annual subscription SKU (annual and monthly price options) and a marketplace listing timeline.
- Share vendor onboarding link / tax W-9 and any marketplace registration steps.
- We’ll need the Redwood legal contact for minor contract questions — please provide point of contact.

Procurement will review the attached quote and follow up with a PO once legal confirms the standard SaaS contract aligns with our guidelines.

Thanks — procurement@lumenai.com
